Barley Hill Primary School
OFSTED Inspection 2025 - "Barley Hill has taken effective action to maintain the standards identified at the previous inspection."
Headteacher’s Welcome Message
Welcome to Barley Hill Primary School. It is a thriving school and one which we are all immensely proud of. We believe that all children are entitled to an education that will enable them to realise their full potential. That this will be achieved in a safe learning environment, where children feel confident to take risks, and know that their efforts will be praised and nurtured.
All children are entitled to a full and enriching education, where first hand experiences, creativity and enjoyment form the basis of successful learning and the development of the whole child. Children at Barley Hill Primary School are encouraged to be active participants in their own learning, to develop resilience and resourcefulness, in order to foster an enquiring mind and a desire for life-long learning.
The school has an excellent range of facilities and benefits from the leadership of committed and enthusiastic staff. Our highly skilled teaching and support staff strive to inspire and value all children as individuals and are dedicated in working in partnership with parents and carers to enable all children to thrive.Mrs Gemma Penny, Headteacher

pageCache.text:
Barley Hill Primary School
S4A Barley Hill Wrap Around Care
Providing trusted, caring and nurturing wrap around care is really important to us at S4A. We’re the first faces at the start of your child’s school day, and the ones waving them off at the end of the day!And we take that responsibility very seriously. We want their wrap around care experience to be a happy one. Full of laughter, creativity, fun and smiles. We want every child to feel safe, involved, engaged and – above all – provide a space for them to be an active part of. In turn, enabling you to feel relaxed knowing they love their time with us.
Here's what to expect:New Breakfast Club TimesOur Breakfast Club starts at 7:30am, giving you that little extra time in the morning. You can choosebetween two sessions:
7:30am–Start of school - £6.958:00am–Start of school - £4.95
And don’t worry — breakfast is served up until 8:15am, so even late risers won’t miss out.
After School Club OptionsWe offer a choice of three booking sessions to suit your schedule:
From end of school day at 3:15pm until 4:30pm - £6.95From end of school day at 3:15pm until 6:00pm - £14.25 From finish time of clubs run by other providers on the school site from 4.15pm until 6.00pm- £8.25
Your child will enjoy a wide range of games, crafts, outdoor fun, and plenty of smiles in a relaxed, safe setting led by our caring team. We also offer a light meal, served at 5:00pm for bookings from 4:30pm onwards — the meal option is already included in your slot when booking, and we’ll take care of the rest so your child finishes their day fed and happy.
How to book & FAQs:We’ve made it super easy for you — simply click on the link and it will take you to two videos showing you how to book on our simple online booking system, as well as a video on some Frequently Asked Questions we receive: https://bit.ly/S4AatBarleyHill
Barley Hill Primary School

Barley Hill Primary School
Governors
Barley Hill Primary School, in common with all maintained schools, is governed by a group of independent people appointed for a fixed term of office, usually four years. The Board comprises of a number of representatives, including elected parent governors, the local authority and the community. The Governing Body focuses on the long-term development and improvement of the school in continuing to ensure that the high standards of learning, achievement and behaviour we have at Barley Hill are maintained and developed. Meetings relating to school finances, the curriculum, the school grounds, staffing and childcare are held with the common purpose of ensuring that the children at Barley Hill Primary School receive the best possible education and make excellent progress!
By working closely with school staff, the Governors play an important role in ensuring that firm foundations are laid for your child's education and that your child has a happy, secure and successful time whilst at primary school.
A message from our Chair of Governors
Dear Parents and Carers
On behalf of the school governors, I warmly invite you to our school. We pride ourselves on providing a safe and nurturing school environment, with children being taught through the 'Barley Hill Way', enabling all children to build on their learning journey and thrive in all aspects of their development.
Our governing body works closely with Mrs Gemma Penny, senior leaders and subject leads to shape our school, ensuring we keep the interests of all pupils at the centre of what we do and that we are educating the whole child.
To find out more about what the role involves, there is useful information on the following website https://www.oxfordshire.gov.uk/residents/our-work-schools/school-governors/governors.
There may be opportunities for parents and carers to become parent governors through the election process and for members of the community to be appointed to co-opted roles. If you feel that this role is for you, then please get in touch with myself KSGovernor@barley-hill.oxon.sch.uk or Mrs Gemma Penny.
I encourage you to explore our website and understand our school community and how we are at the heart of this wonderful community in Thame.
Please click below for further information on the Governors:

Barley Hill Governor Profiles
Jaz works in finance, as Senior Director of International Tax. She is fairly new to school governance, having joined the board of Barley Hill Primary School in 2022, though Jaz has some previous board experience from serving as a pension scheme trustee for 8 years.
Jaz has lived in Oxfordshire for over 20 years, and has a son who attends Barley Hill; he loves school and his class teachers to date have all formed supportive positive relationships with him. Jaz enjoyed her own time at school and believes positive early experiences with plenty of encouragement, exposure to ideas, and excellent teaching will set children up for success. She decided to become a governor to have greater involvement in the school and hopefully use her financial and analytical skills to assist the school on its journey of continuous improvement.
Jaz ran the London Marathon in 2023, and also enjoys football and long walks with their two dogs.
Other roles: Link governor Personal Development and Behaviour and Attitudes
Kayleigh has been a parent governor since May 2022 when her eldest son was in reception. Kayleigh lives with her family in Thame and now has a son and daughter who both enjoy attending Barley Hill School.
During her primary and secondary education, Kayleigh attended many schools abroad as her father was a member of the armed forces. She hopes this experience will allow her to have a broad range of experiences to contribute to her role as governor.
Kayleigh works at the University of Oxford designing and carrying out clinical trials in mothers and babies who are cared for in the NHS. In both her work and governor roles, Kayleigh enjoys making a difference and getting the best outcomes for children and their families.
I am a parent of two children – both of whom attend Barley Hill. I am an Associate Director at the Bodleian Libraries, University of Oxford, where I lead on digital and new collections. Outside of work I enjoy visiting historic houses and going to church. This is my first Governor role – and I am really keen to contribute to the development of Barley Hill.

Mental Health and WellbeingOur Mental Health and Wellbeing Intent
Welcome to the Barley Hill Wellbeing Hub.
It is so important we do what we can to look after our mental wellbeing. Adults and children alike need to be aware of what makes them feel good - better mental health helps all of us…at work, at school, at home, and in the way we feel about ourselves.
Please go to the bottom of the page to find some mindfulness and wellbeing activities for your child to use at home.
Here are five steps to Mental Wellbeing;
You can take the Mind Plan Quiz on the NHS website to discover more ways to feel better. Click here for the Mind Plan Quiz.
We hope for our children to be both physically and emotionally well.
Here are some ideas to promote both areas of wellbeing...
Children and Young People need to do at least 60 minutes of physical activity every day. It keeps bones healthy and encourages muscle strength and flexibility. It is also amazing for keeping us feeling positive and energetic. Here are some exercise ideas to keep children active:
Fun ideas to keep active:
* Have a kitchen disco and enjoy a good boogie!
* Make an obstacle course inside or outside
* Get skipping – skipping ropes are cheap and skipping is a great exercise!
* Who can do the most exercises in a minute – whoever wins gets to choose what you play next i.e. star jumps / sit ups / hops / jumps from side to side
* Who can keep the hula hoop going for the longest – time each other and beat your record the next day
* Treasure hunts around the house/garden
* A nature hunt at the park
Children and their emotions:
Here at Barley Hill Primary School, we promote the use of Zones of Regulation®. We know how important it is for us all to recognise our different emotions and have a ‘tool box’ of strategies to help us cope when we feel angry, tired, worried etc.
Here are some lovely books to help children understand their emotions:
Mindfulness for children:
Mindfulness can help adults and children alike. There is now lots of research that indicates mindfulness can help children improve their abilities to pay attention, to calm down when they are upset and to make better decisions.
Keep it simple. Mindfulness is a big word for young children to understand. Put simply, mindfulness is about awareness - noticing our thoughts, feelings, bodily sensations, and anything that is around us and happening right now.
There are some great apps to support Mindfulness - Headspace, Smiling Mind and Stop, Breathe and Think Kids.
There are also lots of lovely Yoga activities on YouTube, we love Cosmic Kids:
The practice of gratefulness is easy and fun – it also boosts feelings of positivity, connection to others and the world around us, as well as giving us a sense of happiness and calm…it is certainly worth spending time on this practice with our children. Here are some activities, which are both engaging and practical:
* Have a family ‘Grateful’ jar – each day / week add your own note with a picture, word or sentence to show what you are grateful for. You can read them all at the end of the month or year!
* Gratitude photo challenge – encourage children (or have a go yourself) to take pictures of things you are grateful for when you go for a walk or even around your home!
* Write a ‘Gratefulness’ journal. Write three things you are grateful for each day (or draw pictures’ – just before bed is a great time to do this as it calms the mind and ends the day on a positive

pageCache.pageTitle: The Barley Hill Way Curriculum | Barley Hill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Barley Hill Primary School
Educating the whole child, achieved through an inclusive and supportive ethos, with kindness and community at the heart of our provision.
Our Curriculum - The Barley Hill Way
Curriculum Intent
At Barley Hill Primary School, our firmly held belief of ‘Educating the Whole Child’ underpins every aspect of our carefully designed curriculum, which inspires, excites and enthuses our life-long learners –
The Barley Hill Way.
We have a caring, supportive and inclusive learning environment where every child is valued as a learner and citizen. We also value being a prominent and active part of our local community that reflects in our curriculum opportunities.
Our ambitious, broad and rich curriculum, captures the imagination of the children across all subjects, enabling them to be creative, critical thinkers. The varied, stimulating opportunities and skills-based lessons enable the children to connect and build their knowledge progressively over time across all subjects to ambitious end points, ensuring challenge for all and that each child is ready for the next step of their learning through school and become ready to be successful in the real world.
Curriculum Implementation
At Barley Hill, we have used the National Curriculum alongside specialised schemes to ensure that children are taught the full National Curriculum targets across all subjects and are taught key skills and knowledge in a progressive way from EYFS to Year 6. Our curriculum design ensures that pupils can achieve both knowledge and skill. These skills in many subjects revisit key knowledge and skills to further embed these at a more complex level as they move through the school.
We offer a 'Knowledge Engaged' Curriculum. This means that children learn skills alongside knowledge, ensuring that both are explicitly developed. There is a strong emphasis on quality first teaching in order to make the curriculum relevant and meaningful to pupils and for putting knowledge into context.
Curriculum Pedagogy
At Barley Hill Primary School, the curriculum is designed around the spiral curriculum approach, ensuring that concepts are revisited and built upon from the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) through to Year 6. This method allows students to deepen their understanding and skills progressively, with each revisit increasing in complexity.
Key Elements of Barley Hill’s Curriculum Pedagogy:
Curriculum Impact
Teachers assess both the skill and the knowledge in order to assess impact. We have identified key knowledge/skills within the subject areas which, once mastered, will support children in developing further.
The intended impact of our curriculum is that by the end of each academic year, the vast majority of pupils will have sustained mastery of the curriculum content that they have been studying, i.e. they can remember it and are fluent in it. Some pupils will have a greater depth of understanding.
Impact is monitored by senior and subject leaders through lesson observations, learning walks, book scrutinies, pupil voice, assessment data tracking and pupil progress meetings. We also want our pupils to develop as independent, confident, successful learners, with high aspirations, who know how to make a positive contribution to their community and the wider society - mirroring our school motto of ‘Educating the Whole Child’.
